chunk_map.heading: Where the rule could live (H1 + lede)
The file is steady; the agent moves

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 (line 3) names the simulated referent directly: "your `backlog-refinement-rules.md`". chunk 1 (lines 8-10): "the file" (line 8), "the agent runs with the file in context" (line 9), "The file decides" (line 9) all resolve to that chunk-0 naming; "a request", "a teammate", "an issue" are each introduced and used within their own bullet, no dangling pronoun. chunk 2 (lines 15-17): "all three agents" (line 15) resolves to chunk 1's three named bullets (Slack triage / Issue webhook / Scheduled read) — a same-file backward reference, explicitly a NOT-violation under rule 1; "The file" (line 16) and "the file" (line 16) resolve to the same chunk-0 referent; "those rules" (line 17) resolves to the file established as containing rules (chunk 0's `backlog-refinement-rules.md` and chunk 1 line 8's mention of it alongside the thread). Harm this rule guards against — a reader stranded mid-deck unable to find what a word points to — is absent throughout; every referent is nameable at the point of use.

No chunk points at another file by position anywhere in lines 1-18. Every cross-reference is intra-file continuity (line 15's "all three agents" pointing back at chunk 1 — rule 1's territory, not rule 2's). No document is named or located by page position.

chunk 1 carries three self-contained shape descriptions (lines 8-10), each a full claim standalone. chunk 2 carries three bulleted claims (lines 15-17), each self-carrying (a synthesis line, a mechanism line, a naming line). Neither chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

chunk 1 header "Three agents using the file" (line 5): body lists exactly three named agent-shapes (Slack triage / Issue webhook / Scheduled read, lines 8-10), each explicitly using the file — literally true, not contradicted. chunk 2 header "The file is steady; the agent moves" (line 12): line 16 states the steady half almost verbatim ("the file rides along unchanged"), line 17 states the moving half (agents author/read/pass context along) — the chunk's own content never contradicts the header, it substantiates both halves.

Checked all five sub-items against lines 5-18. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triple — chunk 2's three bullets (lines 15-17) open on three different subjects/frames, not a repeated grammatical pattern. No self-grading superlative. No number-plus-retraction (no numerals with a hedge anywhere in the body). No abstraction-noun stack — "wiring choices" (line 16) and "rides along unchanged" (line 16) are concrete engineering phrases, not jargon nouns like "bounded-window reality". Closest candidate for a verb triplet is line 10's "which items want to merge, which want to split, which want to die" — each leg answers "what does this concretely mean?" on its own (three distinct backlog actions); no empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1: three bolded handles, one per bullet (**Slack triage.**, **Issue webhook.**, **Scheduled read.**, lines 8-10), each 2 words, inside the ≲5-word handle cap. This exceeds the plain ≤1-per-slide budget on its face, but the maintainer block's dated accept-note (line 23, "Emphasis pass 2026-07-09... slide 1 keeps bullets with the three shape-name handles... per theory-plan.md § Slide format — emphasis budget + check_slides.md §9") explicitly reconciles this exact passage against this exact rule, and the passage also independently fits the reading-list/menu-slide carve-out (a scanned menu of three usage shapes, one navigational handle per entry). chunk 2: exactly one bolded handle (**Agents build agents.**, line 17), matching the same accept-note's "slide 2 de-bolded except Agents build agents (recurring arc handle, becomes an M6 lecture title)" — squarely within the plain budget.

The file's whole body is two `##`-headed sections plus the H1/lede (lines 1-18) — no phase-less prose section, no prework/supplementary/reference wrapper gap of the kind rule 10 warns against, so nothing here is at risk of the deck-drop failure mode.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 header "Three agents using the file" (line 5) is a catalogue entry naming its subject (three named agent-usage shapes follow), inside the rule's own carve-out for catalogue headers — not a violation even though it reads as a label rather than a claim. chunk 2 header "The file is steady; the agent moves" (line 12) is a genuine declarative claim, and it sits exactly where the rule requires one: the maintainer's own "Lecture meta" note (line 31) names this placement explicitly as "the naming beat, placed AFTER the shapes so it lands as recognition (`check_lectures §1`)". Both headers satisfy the rule on its own terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: None of the three low-value classes present. (a) doctrine restatement: chunk 2's second bullet (line 16, "The file travels. Trigger and runtime are wiring choices; the file rides along unchanged.") is the beat's first and only unpacking of the header's claim, not an Nth recitation, and it names the concrete split (trigger/runtime vs. the file) the header alone doesn't carry. Chunk 2's first bullet (line 15, "Across all three agents, better rules produce better tickets") is a new synthesis across chunk 1's three shapes, not a restatement of anything already said. (b) self-referential design commentary: no line describes the training's own pedagogy to the student. (c) aphorism kicker: no bullet closes the slide by restating the header or an exercise's own point-line as a koan — line 17 ("Agents build agents...") introduces new mechanism (an agent authoring the file another agent reads), not a closing restatement. Each bullet in both chunks adds a distinct move, object, or claim the slide does not already hold.
